title: Kolam Maker
description: A dot-grid drawing pad for making kolam designs. Learners choose a 3 by 3 to 7 by 7 grid of dots (pulli), draw with a mouse or finger, and see each stroke copied with 4-fold rotational symmetry. A computed demo traces a pulli kolam whose line loops around every dot without touching it, using one continuous line on odd grids.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Visual art and craft
Kolam and rangoli
Symmetry
Patterns and symmetry
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Create a symmetric design on a grid of dots in the style of a pulli kolam.
Explain how the dot grid guides where lines go in a kolam.
Explain what 4-fold rotational symmetry is and identify it in a design.
prerequisites: Basic idea of turning a shape around a point
keyQuestions: What job do the dots do in a pulli kolam?
How can one continuous line loop around every dot without touching any?
What makes a design have 4-fold rotational symmetry?
misconceptions: Kolam and rangoli are exactly the same thing.
Kolam designs are drawn freehand without any plan.
Folk art like kolam is less skilled or less mathematical than fine art.
controls: Grid size menu (3 x 3 to 7 x 7 dots)
Draw with mouse or finger on the ground
